Insights & recommendations · October 2026
Insights
1
Cost efficiency
Cost per lead eased to RM14.85 this month, while cost per subscriber rose to RM84.46, the weaker of the two. Conversion slipped to 17.6% from 20.7%, which is the main factor here, more than the cost of the leads themselves.
2
Lead channel mix
WhatsApp Messaging remained the main driver this month, contributing 186 leads, 73% of the total. It was also this month's biggest mover, up 14, so the account is leaning on it more, not less.
3
Conversion funnel health
17.6% of leads became subscribers this month, down 3.1 points from 20.7%, while lead volume grew 8%. The dip sits in the conversion step rather than lead generation, worth a closer look before pushing more spend into the top of the funnel.
4
Spend concentration
Retargeting | Messaging | WA | EN CONTENT accounted for 34% of this month's spend, with a cost per lead running 6% above the account average. Since it's the largest single campaign, even a modest efficiency gain here would have an outsized effect on the account as a whole.
Recommendations
1
Budget allocation
Prospecting | Sales Messaging | WA | In-House Content produced the cheapest leads this month at RM12.43, compared to RM19.89 for Prospecting | Messaging | WA | EN CONTENT, a meaningful gap between two campaigns on the same platform. We'd recommend shifting some budget from the latter into the former next month and watching whether the cost advantage holds as spend increases.
2
Lead engagement quality
43.2% of the leads reached this month replied back the same day, down from 46.8% last month. A same-day reply is usually a sign of stronger intent, so this dip is worth watching, we'd recommend testing a sharper opening message or narrowing the audience toward higher-intent segments to help bring it back up.
3
Creative refresh vs scale
6months-meta-static-messaging-cn was this month's strongest performer, with 50 leads at RM12.37 each. 13 of the account's 24 active creatives are each spending under 2% of budget with little to show for it, we'd recommend shifting that spend toward the top performers and retiring or refreshing the underperforming 13.
4
Video content format
Only 52% of 3-second plays reach the 25% watched mark, the steepest drop in the funnel, and just 10% watch to the end. Since most of the loss happens right at the start, we'd recommend prioritising a stronger opening hook on new creative over changes to the middle or end of the video.
Strategy note · Meta Ads

1. Creative fatigue
Cost per lead has risen from RM11.22 in June and July to RM14.61 from August to October, which points to potential fatigue on our BAU creatives.

2. Cost per reach and targeting
Cost per 1,000 reach has risen from RM34.73 in January to RM108.83 in October, with CPM and frequency climbing too, a sign of audience pool fatigue.

3. Key offer focus test
With the RM48 trial now removed (website conversion offers a 7-day free trial, WhatsApp conversion offers none), the offer itself may be affecting recent results.

  • We’d propose an A/B test of the current offer against the previous RM48 trial to find out.

4. CRM and tracking alignment for website conversion (for discussion)

Insights & recommendations · Google AdsBased on 31 days of data
Insights
1
Spend and traffic
RM974.00 bought 533 clicks over 31 days, at an average CPC of RM1.83 and a 4.36% CTR, with daily spend stepping down from RM49.99 to RM14.01 after the 16 Oct budget cut.
2
Conversions
GA4 recorded 23 conversions at RM42.35 each, against 9.00 Google Ads conversions at RM108.22 each.
3
Brand vs Generic
Brand SEM delivered 74% of Google Ads conversions on 23% of spend, at RM33.52 per conversion against RM321.65 for Generic SEM.
4
Keywords
Four keywords produced all 9.00 Google Ads conversions, led by bookit (5.67) and salon booking software (1.33), while the five highest-cost keywords took 79% of spend.
5
Bidding change
After bidding moved to Maximize Conversions on 27 Oct, Generic SEM clicks fell from 5.5 a day (16 to 26 Oct) to 1.4 (27 to 31 Oct), while Brand SEM rose from 5.4 to 6.8.
Recommendations
1
Keyword spend
We'd recommend reviewing the keywords that spent without a Google Ads conversion, starting with pos system for beauty salon in malaysia (RM152.12) and fresha alternative (RM96.11), which together took 25% of spend.
2
Low search volume
We'd recommend replacing the 26 keywords Google Ads flags as low search volume with higher-volume terms, as they cannot serve ads at their current volume.
3
Ad rank
We'd recommend improving ad rank on Generic SEM ahead of any further budget increase, as 65.40% of its impressions were lost to rank against 25.26% to budget, a gap of 40.1 points.
4
Bid strategy
We'd recommend leaving Maximize Conversions in place for a few more weeks before judging it, as it only took over on 27 Oct and Generic SEM has just 2.33 conversions to learn from.
5
Early data
We'd recommend treating cost per conversion as directional for now, as a sample of nine Google Ads conversions over 31 days is still small.
